Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Signatures → Signature freshness

Signature database freshness

A daily read of each FortiWeb's signature database version that raises a device alert when a box stops updating from FortiGuard — or when its version cannot be read.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Administrator → Signatures → Signature DB freshness per device (URL /signatures/#sig-freshness); scheduled action signature_check

What is it?#

Every FortiWeb downloads its own signature database from FortiGuard; SATOM never carries signatures, not even in a pack. What SATOM does since 3.0 is notice when a box stops updating: the daily scheduled action signature_check reads each FortiWeb's signature database version and records when it last changed, and the alert engine raises a device alert when the database is too old or cannot be read.

What does it do?#

  • Reads, per FortiWeb, only the signature database version — one read-only CLI command over SSH (diagnose system update info) — and the device's own Last Update Date.
  • Re-reads the full signature catalog only when a version changed, instead of hundreds of REST reads every day.
  • Classifies each device as current, stale or unreadable:
  • stale — older than the limit (default 7 days), measured from the device's own last-update time or, when it gives none, from when SATOM saw the version change; or the device reports it never downloaded an update;
  • unreadable — the version could not be read (SSH off, wrong credentials, timeout).
  • Raises a warning in the device alert family: "Signature DB on <device> is stale" or "Signature DB version unreadable on <device>", with the same toggle, routing and cooldown as the other device-health alerts.
  • Skips devices in maintenance.

Requirements#

  • FortiWeb appliances with working SSH credentials (FortiADC and the other products are not checked).
  • The scheduled action signature_check exists. Scheduled actions are data, not code: on a node updated from 2.x, create it once on the primary with sudo satom execute seed actions --yes (daily at 06:15), or on the Scheduled actions page.
  • Alert delivery configured under Email & alerts if you want the finding to reach someone.

Permissions#

The Signatures page needs users.manage. Alerts reach whoever the alert routing sends them to.

How to use#

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM open Administrator → Signatures.
  2. Read the card Signature DB freshness per device: Device, Version, Last update, Checked and Status (current, stale, unreadable). Hover a badge for the reason.
  3. For a stale device, check its FortiGuard connectivity and licence on the appliance; for an unreadable one, its SSH access from SATOM.

Before the action has run, the card says No reading yet — the scheduled action signature_check has not run and shows how to seed it.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
alerts.signature_max_days Age in days after which a signature database is stale. An application setting; 3.0.0 has no field for it on the Settings pages No 7 (default)
Scheduled action signature_check When the daily read runs Yes daily 06:15

Example#

🧪Example — A box that lost FortiGuard

fweb-02 lost its route to FortiGuard after a firewall change. Eight days later the morning signature_check reads the same version with a last update eight days ago: the card shows stale and the alert engine sends Signature DB on fweb-02 is stale to the operations channel.

Result#

  • The state per device is stored as an application setting, so it replicates to the standby with everything else.
  • The finding clears on its own once a later check sees a fresh database.

Troubleshooting#

Every device reads "unreadable"#

Possible causes - SSH is disabled on the appliances or SATOM's credentials do not allow SSH.

Solution 1. Test the SSH console of one appliance from its detail page.

A new lab box reads "stale" right away#

Possible causes - A FortiWeb that never reached FortiGuard reports its last update as the epoch (1969/1970): SATOM treats that as "never updated", which is stale.

Solution 1. Let the box reach FortiGuard, or put it in maintenance.

No alert arrives although the card shows "stale"#

Possible causes - The device alert family is off, or no sink accepts warnings.

Solution 1. Check the alert routing under Email & alerts.

Advanced#

Advanced FortiGuard metadata

When a knowledge pack carries signature metadata (public FortiGuard encyclopedia data: name, severity, category, CVEs, a link), the signature search shows a severity badge and the CVEs next to each id, and signature details add a FortiGuard row. No pack carries it today: FortiGuard's terms do not permit collecting and redistributing that data, so the harvester's enrichment is disabled and the signature-meta section ships empty until it is permitted.
